spec.description: Where your network talks to, and which outside threats it meets.

options.content: Where traffic goes (countries, networks) and which outside threats show up: threat-intel hits, beaconing, malicious TLS, DNS tricks. Country data needs the GeoIP database to be installed.

spec.title: Countries your network talks to
spec.description: Each marker is a country contacted recently, coloured by risk (0-10).

spec.title: Riskiest countries
spec.description: The 10 highest-risk countries by the engine's GeoIP risk score.

properties.value: GeoIP-based risk for traffic to this country/network.

spec.title: All countries (traffic context)
spec.description: Every country your network talks to, risky or not: traffic, devices, DNS activity.

properties.value: How many of your devices talked to it.
DNS lookups per minute resolving there.
Average randomness of the domain names (above ~4.5 looks machine-generated).

spec.title: Threat-intel matches (per hour, by feed)
spec.description: Connections to destinations listed on a threat-intel feed, per rolling hour.

spec.title: Beaconing (per device)
spec.description: Regular, clock-like outbound connections, a classic sign of malware checking in.

spec.title: Malicious TLS fingerprints (JA4)
spec.description: Connections whose TLS handshake matches known malware tooling. Any non-zero value is serious.

spec.title: Malicious TLS fingerprints (JA3, older format)
spec.description: Same idea as JA4, for families only catalogued under the older format.

spec.title: Domain-name randomness (per device)
spec.description: Average randomness of looked-up names. Machine-generated domains (DGA) sit above ~4.5.

spec.title: Lateral movement events (per hour)
spec.description: A device probing several of your other devices. Almost always worth investigating.

spec.title: Honeypot probes (per hour)
spec.description: Contacts to a decoy address you configured. Only meaningful if you set one up.

spec.title: Encrypted-DNS bypass (per device)
spec.description: Connections to DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers that go around your Pi-hole.
